title: Python top-level statements must be wrapped in func main
description: Python executes top-level statements at module load. Go only allows declarations at file scope; executable statements must live inside a function, typically main(). Emit package main, gather imports, then wrap the procedural body in func main().
avoid_pattern:
package main
import "fmt"
n := 0
fmt.Scan(&n)
fmt.Println(n)
compile_error_signatures: syntax error: non-declaration statement outside function body

title: Unused imports fail go build
description: Python allows imports to sit unused. Go treats any unused import as a fatal compile error. Only import packages actually referenced; when you add an import speculatively, either use it or drop it before emitting.
python_signal: 'import x' retained after logic was simplified; leftover import stubs remain in the translation

routing_hints.remediation: drop any import whose selector does not appear in the file

title: Declared but unused local variables fail go build
description: Python silently tolerates unused locals. Go rejects them with 'declared and not used'. Either consume the value, discard it with _, or remove the declaration entirely.
python_signal: locals that Python assigns but never reads
go_pattern:
_, err := fmt.Fscan(reader, &n)
if err != nil { return }

title: Go requires every return value to be captured
description: Python ignores return values silently; Go demands each one be assigned or discarded with _. fmt.Fscan, strconv.Atoi, and similar stdlib APIs return multiple values and will fail compile when treated like Python single-return calls.
python_signal: call site treats a multi-return Go API as if it returned a single value
go_pattern:
n, err := strconv.Atoi(line)
if err != nil { return }
avoid_pattern: n := strconv.Atoi(line) // compile error: assignment mismatch
compile_error_signatures: assignment mismatch: 1 variable but fmt.Fscan returns 2 values
not enough arguments in call to strconv.Atoi

title: Do not shadow stdlib package names with parameters or locals
description: A Go parameter or local named strings, sort, strconv, math, or fmt blocks access to that package selector. If the signature already uses one of those names, rename internal variables and avoid assuming strings.Join means the package.
python_signal: the provided Go signature already binds a common stdlib package name
compile_error_signatures: X has no field or method Join
X has no field or method HasPrefix

title: Do not invent Go stdlib APIs or omit required helpers
description: Python helper names and stdlib organization do not map directly to Go. References like math.Gcd or strings.Reverse do not exist in the Go standard library, and helper functions mentioned in the logic must actually be emitted in the file.
python_signal: a Python helper or stdlib convenience call is assumed to have a same-named Go equivalent
avoid_pattern:
import "math"
g := math.Gcd(a, b) // compile error: undefined: math.Gcd

title: Never import third-party Go modules
description: The evaluator compiles each translation in a fresh module with no network and no go.mod edits. Any github.com/... or golang.org/x/... import fails at build time. Use only the standard library; if functionality is missing, implement it inline.
python_signal: problem tempts the model toward a popular Go third-party helper library
go_pattern: // implement the needed helper inline using only standard library code
compile_error_signatures: no required module provides package github.com/
no required module provides package golang.org/x/

title: Go has no implicit numeric or string conversions
description: Python coerces int, float, and str on demand. Go requires explicit conversions such as int(x), float64(x), string(rune), and strconv.Itoa. Mixed int/float arithmetic or number-to-string concatenation must be made explicit.
python_signal: arithmetic mixing int and float literals; concatenating numbers into strings
compile_error_signatures: cannot use X as Y value in argument to

title: Python input() semantics do not survive the naive port to Go
description: Python input() reads one line as a string; common idioms split on whitespace and call int(). Go ports need a consistent token reader such as bufio.Scanner with ScanWords or fmt.Fscan. Mis-pairing scanner tokens with loop counts causes panics and wrong output.
python_signal: input().split(), map(int, input().split()), or loops that read N records
go_pattern:
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(os.Stdin)
scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 1024), 1<<20)
scanner.Split(bufio.ScanWords)
readInt := func() int { scanner.Scan(); v, _ := strconv.Atoi(scanner.Text()); return v }
avoid_pattern: fmt.Scan(&n) in a loop over tokenized input without a consistent reader contract
runtime_error_signatures: panic: runtime error: index out of range
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range

title: Reproduce Python print formatting exactly
description: Python print uses a single-space separator and trailing newline by default. Go's fmt.Println and default float formatting are not always byte-equivalent. Match stdout exactly: separator, newline, and float formatting must mirror the Python behavior required by the tests.
python_signal: print() with multiple args, sep=, end=, or float-to-string formatting

title: Rewrite Python negative indices explicitly in Go
description: Go does not support negative indices like xs[-1]. Any negative subscript must be rewritten explicitly with len(xs)-k before indexing.
python_signal: negative subscript such as xs[-1] or xs[-2]

title: Copy a slice before mutating when Python semantics require an independent list
description: Python slices like xs[:] create a new list. In Go, assigning or passing a slice usually aliases the same backing array. If the source semantics require an independent copy before mutation, copy explicitly.
python_signal: slice copy expressions such as xs[:] followed by mutation of the copied value
avoid_pattern:
dup := xs
dup[0] = 1 // mutates xs too

title: Do not rely on Go map iteration order
description: Python dict-based logic may depend on insertion or sorted order. Go map iteration order is randomized. If output or traversal order matters, maintain a separate ordered key slice or sort keys explicitly.
python_signal: dictionary construction or iteration where output order matters

title: Preserve Python sorting tie behavior
description: Python's sorted is stable. If the translation sorts by a derived key and equal keys must retain original order, use a stable Go sort or decorate with original indices. Otherwise compile-clean Go can still fail tests.
python_signal: sorted(...) or .sort() where ties matter to the expected output

title: Python floor division with negatives is not Go integer division
description: Python // floors toward negative infinity. Go integer division truncates toward zero. If operands can be negative, direct translation of // to / changes semantics and can produce wrong answers.
python_signal: use of // where operands may be negative
avoid_pattern: q := a / b // wrong when a and b have opposite signs and remainder != 0

title: Return an empty slice when the contract expects a sequence result
description: Python returns [] for an empty result, not None. When the Go signature returns []T and the logical result is empty, prefer []T{} unless nil is explicitly acceptable in the benchmark contract.
python_signal: empty list literal returned from a function with slice return type

provenance.notes: high precision only when paired with explicit empty-list return and slice signature
